personas.name: Simplifier
personas.perspective: Complexity reduction, scope minimization, essential features only

insights: Core value proposition: Enable individual users to organize tasks with secure personal data storage
Primary user segment: Individual productivity users seeking simple, reliable task management
Key differentiator: Simplicity over feature bloat - focus on core todo functionality with authentication
Success depends on seamless authentication UX and zero data loss
Scope is appropriately constrained for MVP - no team collaboration, no integrations, no advanced features
recommendations: Prioritize authentication flow polish - this is the user's first impression and trust anchor
Implement data persistence validation early to prevent catastrophic data loss scenarios
Add basic task filtering (active/completed) before launch - users expect this baseline functionality
Consider password reset flow as table stakes for authentication - users will lock themselves out
Build task creation/editing as atomic operations with optimistic UI for perceived performance
risks: Authentication complexity could delay MVP - recommend social auth (OAuth) or passwordless for simplicity
Data loss during beta would destroy user trust - need robust backup/recovery strategy
Performance degradation with large task lists (>1000 items) could trigger negative reviews
Scope creep pressure for features (tags, priorities, due dates) - must defend MVP boundaries
Security vulnerability in auth system would be catastrophic for user data confidentiality

insights: Architecture is well-suited for MVP - simple layered design (presentation, API, business logic, data) supports quick iteration
MVP scope supports horizontal scaling through stateless API design - ready for cloud-native deployment
Three-tier architecture enables independent frontend/backend development and testing in parallel
Database schema is simple and normalized, supporting future indexing and query optimization without refactoring
Session management strategy (stateless JWT preferred) aligns with horizontal scaling and distributed deployment
API-first design enables future mobile client support without backend changes
Monolithic deployment is appropriate for MVP - simplifies DevOps complexity while maintaining separation of concerns
recommendations: Use stateless JWT tokens with refresh token rotation for session management - supports horizontal scaling and simplifies deployment
Implement optimistic locking (version fields) on task updates to prevent concurrent update conflicts without complex distributed transactions
Design API to use pagination by default (limit/offset) for task list queries - prevents N+1 queries and memory issues as user task count grows
Establish API versioning strategy (v1) from start - protects frontend/mobile clients during backend evolution
Use single database with connection pooling for MVP - revisit sharding only if user base exceeds performance benchmarks
Implement structured logging (JSON) from day one - essential for production debugging and performance analysis
Design data model to support future filtering without schema changes - add 'tags' field as nullable but empty for MVP
Use database transactions for multi-step operations (create task + audit log) to prevent inconsistency
risks: N+1 query problems if task list endpoint doesn't paginate - could cause severe performance degradation at scale
Concurrent update conflicts without optimistic locking could cause data corruption or user frustration
Weak password hashing (MD5, SHA1) would create security vulnerability - must use bcrypt/argon2 with salt
Storing session data in memory (no Redis) limits horizontal scaling - recommend lightweight Redis for MVP+ phase
Missing database indices on frequently-queried fields (user_id, created_at) would cause table scans and slow queries
Uncontrolled session token lifetime could leave abandoned sessions consuming memory/resources
API without rate limiting on auth endpoints exposes brute force attack surface
Cross-origin request issues if frontend and backend deployed separately without proper CORS configuration

simplifications.current: Email-based password reset with token expiration, email service integration, multiple endpoints
simplifications.simplified: Eliminate entirely - users can create new account if locked out. Add in v2 if user feedback demands it
simplifications.savings: 24 hours development + $10/month email service + reduced complexity in users table (no reset token fields)

simplifications.current: Email verification flow with verification emails, email_verified fields, verify-email endpoint
simplifications.simplified: Eliminate - accept any valid email format. Add verification only if spam/abuse becomes issue
simplifications.savings: 16 hours development + reduced email service usage

simplifications.current: Full audit trail with JSONB old/new values, entity tracking, immutable append-only table
simplifications.simplified: Use application logging for errors/issues. Add audit table in v2 if compliance requires it
simplifications.savings: 20 hours development + database storage + query complexity

simplifications.current: Separate refresh_tokens table with token hashing, expiration, revocation tracking. 15min access + 7day refresh tokens
simplifications.simplified: Single JWT token with 24-hour expiration. Re-login after 24 hours. Eliminates entire table and refresh endpoint
simplifications.savings: 16 hours development + simplified session management + one less database table

simplifications.current: Version field on tasks table, concurrent update conflict detection and handling
simplifications.simplified: Last-write-wins for MVP. Single user editing own tasks rarely has conflicts. Add if users report issues
simplifications.savings: 12 hours development + simpler update logic + one less field per task

simplifications.current: Collect and store user names, profile management endpoints (GET/PUT /users/profile)
simplifications.simplified: Email only for authentication. No profile management needed for todo app
simplifications.savings: 8 hours development + 2 fewer database fields + eliminated user service endpoints

simplifications.current: Optional 1000-character description field with validation, UI form field, database storage
simplifications.simplified: Title only (200 chars). Most todos don't need descriptions. Add in v2 if requested
simplifications.savings: 6 hours development + simpler forms + reduced storage

simplifications.current: Soft delete on users and tasks tables, WHERE deleted_at IS NULL in all queries, quarterly archival
simplifications.simplified: Hard deletes with confirmation dialog. Simpler queries, no archival process needed
simplifications.savings: 8 hours development + simpler data model + faster queries

simplifications.current: Edit task title and description with save/cancel, validation, last modified tracking
simplifications.simplified: Defer to v2. Users can delete and recreate task for MVP. Focus on core create/complete/delete flow

simplifications.current: Winston JSON logging, DataDog/CloudWatch integration, Grafana dashboards, log aggregation
simplifications.simplified: Console logging + cloud provider default monitoring (free tier). Add advanced monitoring post-launch if needed

simplifications.current: express-rate-limit on auth endpoints (5 attempts/15min) and API endpoints (100 req/min)
simplifications.simplified: Defer to v2. Cloud provider DDoS protection sufficient for MVP with limited users

simplifications.current: Checkbox UI, different token expiration logic, additional session management complexity
simplifications.simplified: Single 24-hour session for everyone. Eliminates checkbox and branching session logic

simplifications.current: Filter UI tabs (All/Active/Completed), task counts, filter state persistence, API filtering support
simplifications.simplified: Defer filtering UI to v2. Show all tasks in simple list. Client-side filtering can be added quickly if needed

simplifications.current: Full accessibility audit, ARIA labels, screen reader testing, keyboard nav for all features
simplifications.simplified: Basic semantic HTML + keyboard support for main actions. Full AA compliance in v2

simplifications.current: Track timestamps for analytics - last login, task completion time, etc.

consolidations.into: Eliminate entirely - no profile management needed for todo app

infrastructure_simplifications.simplified: Eliminate - no password reset or verification emails needed

infrastructure_simplifications.risk: low - acceptable performance for MVP traffic levels

risk_assessment.overall_recommendation: PROCEED - simplifications significantly reduce complexity while maintaining core value proposition. All medium-risk items have clear v2 migration paths

backend.description: API must follow REST conventions with proper HTTP methods and status codes
Stateless JWT tokens with refresh token rotation. Access tokens expire in 15 minutes, refresh tokens in 7 days
backend.implementation: jsonwebtoken library with secure cookie storage for refresh tokens

backend.description: Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12+) with random salt. Minimum 8 characters enforced
Multi-step operations wrapped in transactions to guarantee consistency
Task list queries use pagination (default 50 items/page, max 100). Indexed queries on user_id, created_at
Auth endpoints limited to 5 failed attempts/15 min per IP. API endpoints limited to 100 req/min per user
All inputs validated server-side for type, length, format. Sanitized to prevent SQL injection and XSS
Consistent error responses with error codes, messages, and request IDs for debugging
JSON-formatted logs with request ID, user ID, timestamp, level, message. Centralized log aggregation ready
API routes prefixed with version (v1). Supports future API evolution without breaking clients

frontend.description: Application functional on mobile (320px+) and desktop. Touch-friendly UI with 44px+ tap targets

frontend.description: Form validation before API call. Real-time feedback on password strength and email format

frontend.description: User-friendly error messages. Network errors show retry option. Auth errors redirect to login

database.description: 3NF normalization. Users and tasks in separate tables with proper foreign keys

infrastructure.description: All traffic encrypted. HSTS header with 1-year max-age. TLS 1.2 minimum

architecture.rationale: Simplicity for MVP while maintaining separation of concerns. Stateless API enables horizontal scaling

architectureDecisions.rationale: Supports horizontal scaling without session server. Simpler deployment model for MVP. Refresh tokens provide security while maintaining statelessness
architectureDecisions.tradeoffs: No server-side token revocation capability (accept for MVP). Logout requires client to discard token and refresh token must be revoked in DB
architectureDecisions.implementation: Access token (15 min) + Refresh token (7 days) in secure HTTP-only cookie

architectureDecisions.rationale: ACID transactions prevent data inconsistency. Relational model fits simple schema. Managed database removes operational burden
architectureDecisions.tradeoffs: No horizontal scaling of database (revisit if >100k users). Requires connection pooling. Single point of failure (mitigate with backups)
architectureDecisions.implementation: PostgreSQL 13+ on managed cloud (RDS/Cloud SQL). Connection pool max 20. Daily backups with point-in-time recovery

architectureDecisions.rationale: Simpler operations model for MVP team. Single codebase reduces coordination overhead. Stateless design allows horizontal scaling of API tier
architectureDecisions.tradeoffs: Cannot scale auth and task services independently. Code must be deployed as unit. Harder to change single service later
architectureDecisions.implementation: Single Express.js app with modular structure. Easy to extract services later without code duplication

architectureDecisions.rationale: Prevents conflicts when two users edit same task. Simpler than distributed locks. Acceptable for MVP user base
architectureDecisions.tradeoffs: Users may see 'conflict' error and need to retry. No automatic conflict resolution. Database version field adds complexity
architectureDecisions.implementation: Version field in tasks table. Client sends version with update. DB checks version before update

architectureDecisions.rationale: Prevents accidental data loss. Enables recovery for support. Maintains audit trail of all data
architectureDecisions.tradeoffs: Must filter deleted_at IS NULL in all queries (use repository pattern). Storage overhead for deleted records. Complicates unique constraints
architectureDecisions.implementation: deleted_at timestamp field. Repository methods filter soft-deleted records by default. Quarterly data archival to cold storage
